turns.en: You have said in the past you would consider an IPO in the first half of 2027. Is that still fair game?
turns.zh: 你过去说过会考虑在 2027 年上半年 IPO。这个计划还作数吗？

turns.en: 2028 is our mental model. Business is progressing faster because we just crossed a billion. So if the business progress sustains, we might consider filing sooner. Public markets force you to be more disciplined, more rigorous, and Perplexity will not be the last IPO.
turns.zh: 2028 年是我们的心理预期。业务进展比预期更快，因为我们刚刚突破了 10 亿美元。所以如果业务进展持续，我们可能会考虑更早提交申请。公开市场会迫使你更加自律、更加严谨，而 Perplexity 不会是最后一个 IPO。

turns.en: Delighted to be here with Aravind, the CEO of Perplexity, and I'm equally delighted to have Stephanie as a co-host, Stephanie Beebe, star portfolio manager at T. Rowe Price, old friend, and ran track at Swarthmore with my wife, Becky. So Stephanie, please take us away.
turns.zh: 很高兴能和 Perplexity 的 CEO Aravind 在一起，我也同样高兴能请到 Stephanie 作为联合主持人，Stephanie Beebe，T. Rowe Price 的明星投资组合经理，老朋友，曾和我妻子 Becky 一起在 Swarthmore 跑田径。那么 Stephanie，请开始吧。

turns.en: Great. Thank you for that introduction, Gavin, and thank you for inviting me. Aravind, we really appreciate you joining for this and it's my pleasure to have this discussion with you.
turns.zh: 太好了。谢谢你的介绍，Gavin，也谢谢你邀请我。Aravind，我们非常感谢你参与这次对话，我很高兴能和你讨论。

turns.en: Thank you for having me here.
turns.zh: 谢谢你们邀请我来。

turns.en: Of course. We have a broad audience in the room. We have investors, we have Perplexity users, we have potential users, we have members of the wealth industry, we have fellow founders. What do you want this audience to take away about Perplexity AI today?
turns.zh: 当然。在座有广泛的听众。我们有投资者、Perplexity 用户、潜在用户、财富行业人士，还有同行创始人。你希望这些听众今天对 Perplexity AI 有什么样的了解？

turns.en: Perplexity started off as a first ever product that reimagined what search could be in the age of LLMs. So we basically created this category of an answer engine with verified sources, trustworthy citations, and all that. But we basically build the foundations for something far bigger than what just giving answers to questions can be, which is accurate AI. And citations is just the start of doing something that fundamentally is required to make agents really trustworthy and reliable for the enterprise. So most recently, earlier this year, we launched this product called Perplexity Computer. Towards the end of last year, a lot of people thought we were dead, like there's no business opportunity for us ahead because they really thought that the world has moved on to coding agents and search is dead and it's old technology. But what people didn't really quite realize is that, unless you can really make every single step an agent decides which tool to pick over the repository of tools, or which files to look at, or which paragraphs in these files, or what sources from the web to use, which connectors, which tools each and every step in an agent race is basically a search problem. And who's really well positioned to do that orchestration? A company like us that's not married to any model that really just does what the user cares about, which is get the work done for them. And that's what we launched in February this year called Perplexity Computer. And our revenue basically 4.7X year over year because of that one single product. And today our focus is all about finishing work for businesses with this product. And you know that multi-model orchestration and getting work done for people is our entire focus today.
turns.zh: Perplexity 最初是第一个重新构想 LLM 时代搜索可能是什么样子的产品。所以我们基本上创造了答案引擎这个类别，带有经过验证的来源、可信的引用等等。但我们实际上是在为比仅仅回答问题更宏大的东西奠定基础，那就是准确的 AI。而引用只是开始，从根本上说，这是让智能体真正值得信赖和可靠所必需的。所以最近，今年早些时候，我们推出了这款名为 Perplexity Computer 的产品。去年年底，很多人认为我们死了，好像我们前面没有商业机会了，因为他们真的认为世界已经转向编码智能体，搜索已死，是旧技术。但人们没有真正意识到的是，除非你能真正让智能体做出的每一步决定——选择哪个工具、查看哪些文件、文件中的哪些段落、使用网络上的哪些来源、哪些连接器、哪些工具——智能体竞赛中的每一步基本上都是一个搜索问题。而谁真正有能力做好这种编排？像我们这样的公司，不绑定任何模型，真正只做用户关心的事，那就是为他们完成工作。这就是我们今年二月推出的 Perplexity Computer。我们的收入基本上同比增长了 4.7 倍，就是因为这一个产品。今天我们的重点完全是通过这个产品为企业完成工作。你知道，多模型编排和为人完成工作是我们今天的全部重点。

turns.en: Is it fair to say that Perplexity is building sort of the operating system for AI workers? Is that a fair way to characterize it?
turns.zh: 可以说 Perplexity 正在构建某种 AI 工作者的操作系统吗？这样描述公平吗？

turns.en: It's fair. Operating systems typically orchestrate processes, memory, files. That's exactly what AI is doing. AI is changing what the definition of a computer is. Computers used to refer to people. Elon spoke about this on X at one point where astronomers used to have apprentices, human apprentices who used to be called computers. The job was computer. Except over time that started being done by machines. But now computers are becoming smart. Instead of programming them with specific instructions, you're getting to program them with objectives, natural language objectives. So what you really want a computer to do for you is basically do any task that a human being is sitting on a physical computer, except AI does the task on disposable computers on the cloud, sandboxes, orchestrating across your files, your connectors, multiple different models. Use whatever models are needed for different parts of the task and just get the work done. Nobody has the mind to understand like, oh, these many tokens are going to these models or like these models are good for this specific category of tokens. All that stuff is like irrelevant to the user. At the end of the day, the ROI is realized if you get real work done that's worth certain amount of like labor dollars per hour. And that's really what our positioning is to be.
turns.zh: 公平。操作系统通常编排进程、内存、文件。这正是 AI 在做的事。AI 正在改变计算机的定义。计算机过去指的是人。Elon 曾在 X 上谈到，天文学家过去有学徒，人类学徒被称为“计算机”。工作就是计算机。只是随着时间的推移，这开始由机器完成。但现在计算机变得智能了。你不是用具体指令编程，而是用目标、自然语言目标来编程。所以你真正希望计算机为你做的，基本上是做任何人类坐在物理计算机前做的任务，只不过 AI 在云端的可丢弃计算机、沙盒上完成任务，编排你的文件、连接器、多个不同模型。使用任务不同部分所需的任何模型，然后完成工作。没有人有心力去理解，哦，这么多 token 会流向这些模型，或者这些模型适合这类 token。所有这些对用户来说都无关紧要。归根结底，如果你完成了真正的工作，价值相当于一定金额的每小时劳动力，ROI 就实现了。这就是我们的定位。

turns.en: If I recall, you said Perplexity is at a billion run rate ARR, surpassed that. You reached a billion ARR, I think in with 1/5 the cash burn of Anthropic, if I remember correctly. Um can you talk about how your products are differentiated compared to Anthropic and ChatGPT? Uh specifically you brought up Perplexity computer. How does that compare to what is your technological advantage compared to Claude co work and ChatGPT work?
turns.zh: 如果我没记错，你说过 Perplexity 的 ARR 达到 10 亿美元运行率，已经超过了。你达到了 10 亿美元 ARR，我想是用了 Anthropic 五分之一的现金消耗，如果我没记错的话。嗯，你能谈谈你的产品与 Anthropic 和 ChatGPT 相比有何不同吗？呃，特别是你提到了 Perplexity Computer。与 Claude CoWork 和 ChatGPT Work 相比，你的技术优势是什么？

turns.en: So our advantage is in accuracy and orchestration. So accuracy is because we are a search company. So we have the foundations. We have our own index. We have the best index with the exception of Google. I think we have the best index among every single player in AI. And that's because we've been building it for like four years now. Trillion web pages. We have all the primitives to let coding agents access that index in real time. So that obviously contributes to us being really good at areas where accuracy is table stakes, finance, health, any kind of research and any workflow that an analyst does, Perplexity is really good at that. Now the other part which is pretty important too is orchestration. It doesn't matter to us what is the best model at any moment in time. It could be Gemini Carbon, it could be Claude Opus, it could be GPT Astra or Sol, it could be Grok. It really doesn't matter. It could be an open weight model like DeepSeek or GLM Flash. Anytime any part of the AI ecosystem improves, Perplexity improves. So every time there's an actual advancement in AI, the company that produced the advancement is happy and Perplexity is also happy. So we're not actually worried about progress being made in open weights. We're not lobbying for banning open weight models. We're also not against Frontier Labs. We actually benefit from Frontier Labs improving. So that is that unique model neutral orchestration positioning that the labs cannot actually adopt. And you could argue like Google's rolling out Claude inside Gemini Enterprise and things like that. There's some forms of it happening and Elon's also talked about how like Grok bot's going to use Opus. But this really puts into question like if that is the fundamental right idea, ours is the most capital efficient way to do that. We're not actually building gigantic data centers. We don't have trillion dollars in compute commitments. Our burn is like pretty relatively low. Our gross margins are like 56%.
turns.zh: 我们的优势在于准确性和编排。准确性是因为我们是一家搜索公司。我们有基础。我们有自己的索引。除了 Google，我们拥有最好的索引。我认为我们在 AI 领域的每个玩家中拥有最好的索引。这是因为我们已经构建了大约四年。万亿网页。我们拥有所有原语，让编码智能体实时访问该索引。所以这显然有助于我们在准确性是基本要求的领域表现出色，金融、健康、任何类型的研究以及分析师做的任何工作流，Perplexity 都非常擅长。现在另一个非常重要的部分是编排。在任何时刻哪个模型最好对我们来说并不重要。可能是 Gemini Carbon，可能是 Claude Opus，可能是 GPT Astra 或 Sol，可能是 Grok。真的不重要。可能是像 DeepSeek 或 GLM Flash 这样的开放权重模型。任何时候 AI 生态系统的任何部分有所改进，Perplexity 都会改进。所以每次 AI 有实际进步，产生进步的公司高兴，Perplexity 也高兴。所以我们实际上不担心开放权重的进展。我们不游说禁止开放权重模型。我们也不反对前沿实验室。我们实际上从前沿实验室的改进中受益。所以这就是那种独特的模型中立编排定位，实验室实际上无法采用。你可能会说 Google 在 Gemini Enterprise 中推出 Claude 之类的。有一些形式正在发生，Elon 也谈过 Grok bot 将使用 Opus。但这真的让人质疑这是否是根本正确的想法，我们的是最资本高效的方式。我们实际上没有建造巨大的数据中心。我们没有万亿美元的算力承诺。我们的消耗相对较低。我们的毛利率约为 56%。

turns.en: So like our ability to just be extremely capital efficient, be model neutral, and get real work done for people is basically the differentiation.
turns.zh: 所以，我们能够做到极高的资本效率、保持模型中立，并真正为用户完成实际工作，这基本上就是我们的差异化所在。

turns.en: Can you just talk about—I would guess that you are sensitive to competition and fragmentation at the model layer, and the more competitive it is, the better for you. Like, over the last nine months, can you talk about what's the highest any one model has had as a percentage of the tokens that you processed? What's the distribution? Just give us a sense of how many different models you use, where you are right now, maybe what a historic peak was.
turns.zh: 你能不能谈谈——我猜你对模型层的竞争和碎片化很敏感，而且竞争越激烈对你越有利。比如在过去九个月里，你能谈谈任何一个模型在你处理的 token 中所占的最高百分比是多少吗？分布是怎样的？请给我们一个大致概念：你们用了多少种不同的模型，目前的情况如何，也许还有历史峰值是多少。

turns.en: Yeah. The vanilla Perplexity product that just gives you fast answers—about two, three months ago we started routing almost every single request, whether it's a paid user or a non-paid user, to a model that we train ourselves. It's been post-trained on top of like DeepSeek and GLM. We're very good at post-training. We've been investing in our own post-training infrastructure, RL infrastructure, environments, measuring tool call error rates. That itself has saved us like 100 million a year instead of paying like GPT-5 or some other frontier model for fast, quick answers. Now, on the agent side where you actually spin up sandboxes and do real work, which is like things like Perplexity Computer—today Opus 5.5 is the best model. And we've been post-training our own version with GLM. We are lagging behind there just like every other lab on the planet for one simple capability that Opus has, which is real trajectory efficiency. It's not about the cost per token. It's about the cost for the entire agent race, cost for the session itself. And models like Opus are so efficient at making the right tool calls so that they don't waste user time. And that's the capability that we want to hill climb on. And the only way to actually do that is to actually collect a lot of prompts in production, build environments based on that, and do real RL, which is what we are really investing in. We announced our own frontier research lab. That's what we're going to really focus on, which is building the right set of environments, building the right set of evals, and hill climbing on those with RL.
turns.zh: 是的。普通的 Perplexity 产品只提供快速答案——大约两三个月前，我们开始将几乎每一个请求，无论是付费用户还是非付费用户，都路由到我们自己训练的模型上。它是在 DeepSeek 和 GLM 之上进行后训练的。我们非常擅长后训练。我们一直在投资自己的后训练基础设施、强化学习基础设施、环境，并测量工具调用的错误率。这本身每年为我们节省了约 1 亿美元，而不是付钱给 GPT-5 或其他前沿模型来提供快速答案。现在，在智能体方面，当你真正启动沙盒并完成实际工作时，比如 Perplexity Computer 这类产品——目前 Opus 5.5 是最好的模型。我们一直在用 GLM 后训练我们自己的版本。我们在这方面落后于地球上其他所有实验室，原因很简单：Opus 拥有的一项能力，即真正的轨迹效率。这不是关于每个 token 的成本，而是关于整个智能体运行的成本，即会话本身的成本。像 Opus 这样的模型在做出正确的工具调用方面非常高效，因此不会浪费用户时间。这就是我们想要攀登的能力。而要做到这一点，唯一的方法就是在生产环境中收集大量提示，基于这些构建环境，并进行真正的强化学习，这正是我们正在大力投资的。我们宣布了自己的前沿研究实验室。这将是我们真正专注的方向：构建正确的环境集合、正确的评估集合，并用强化学习在这些方面攀登。

turns.en: What percentage of queries today is that Opus 5.5 as a percentage of tokens?
turns.zh: 今天 Opus 5.5 处理的查询占 token 的百分比是多少？

turns.en: Agentic probably 60 to 70%.
turns.zh: 智能体方面大概是 60% 到 70%。

turns.en: Okay, and is that about as high as any one model has been in Perplexity over the last year?
turns.zh: 好的，那这大约是过去一年里 Perplexity 中任何一个模型达到的最高水平吗？

turns.en: Yes.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: And when you say you're going to put a frontier lab, this is post-training.
turns.zh: 你说要建立一个前沿实验室，这是后训练。

turns.en: This is post-training. Post-training only. Yes. We're not in the business of pre-training because pre-training—not doing our own pre-training is one of the reasons we are able to be capital efficient.
turns.zh: 这是后训练。仅限后训练。是的。我们不做预训练，因为预训练——不自己做预训练正是我们能够保持资本效率的原因之一。

turns.en: How do you think, maybe just stepping back, how do you think the business model for Perplexity, Anthropic, OpenAI evolves over the next 5 years? You're talking about the importance of the frontier lab. You just started that. Presumably you'll be investing in new products and applications. As we talk about moving and focusing on the application layer, what are you selling in 5 years? What does that product look like? Is it a product suite? It's application. I suspect we won't be talking about price per token, but like to hear your view.
turns.zh: 退一步看，你认为 Perplexity、Anthropic、OpenAI 的商业模式在未来 5 年会如何演变？你谈到了前沿实验室的重要性。你刚刚开始做那个。想必你会投资于新产品和应用。当我们谈论转向并专注于应用层时，5 年后你们卖什么？那个产品是什么样子？是一个产品套件吗？是应用。我猜我们不会再谈论每 token 的价格，但想听听你的看法。

turns.en: Firstly, I'll start by saying five years is really really long in AI. It's like the equivalent of 10 to 15, I would say, the rate at which things are moving. If you'd ask anybody last year at an event like this what's going to happen, it's very unlikely they predicted the revenue ramp of coding agents. And so just to be that—you know, you have to have that humility about this question. My prediction is that a lot more people will be entrepreneurial. There's going to be very little barriers to having an idea and have an AI spin up a business for you. Today you have expensive AIs that a few people can afford that can be persistent teammates. We launched a product called Perplexity Teammates, which basically puts something like Perplexity Computer with a persistent sandbox running all the time for you with a specific role so you can have it do proactive tasks. But that's expensive, so very few people can afford it. Now eventually you're going to be able to do things like, okay, I have this business idea and I don't even know how to set up something and go get users and go figure out monetization and go optimize my funnels and advertise it. You're going to be able to set up an organization that just does this for you, autonomous businesses. Now I don't really know when it's going to happen, but it's definitely going to happen in the next five years. So those are the kind of ideas that we are really excited about pursuing on the application layer. As for what the frontier labs are going to do, they're going to hill climb more on coding capabilities. It's very clear that that's a very reliable way to make progress in models. And all that progress in coding capabilities is going to translate to pursuing applications like I just described because fundamentally when you go to code mode and expose your harness, it's all about exposing primitives to coding agents. So that's your job. So when you build the infrastructure, when you build the right primitives, you can hill climb on all the capabilities that labs are going to keep producing. Now, on things outside of coding, I believe they're going to make really good advances in designing chips, building robots, and designing drugs. And maybe there's a role for application layer companies to play there if, you know, they're very good at the last mile problem, running field tests with labs, or being actually able to deploy robots in factories, or having a lot of data from fabs that allow you to close the loop on real physical measurements and testing because a lot of things can work in simulation when you build chips, but don't actually have to work when you put it all together in a rack. So there might be opportunities for application layer companies there that work together with frontier labs to actually, you know, get the chips that they design in real production.
turns.zh: 首先，我想说五年在 AI 领域是非常非常长的时间。按照事物发展的速度，我会说相当于 10 到 15 年。如果你去年在这样的活动上问任何人会发生什么，他们不太可能预测到编码智能体的收入增长。所以对此——你知道，你必须对这个问题的答案保持谦逊。我的预测是，会有更多的人成为创业者。拥有一个想法并让 AI 为你创办企业，将几乎没有障碍。今天你有昂贵的 AI，只有少数人负担得起，可以作为持久队友。我们推出了一款名为 Perplexity Teammates 的产品，它基本上把类似 Perplexity Computer 的东西与一个持续运行的沙盒结合起来，为你扮演特定角色，这样你就可以让它执行主动任务。但那很昂贵，所以很少有人能负担得起。最终你将能够做这样的事情：好吧，我有这个商业想法，我甚至不知道如何建立公司、获取用户、弄清楚盈利模式、优化我的漏斗并做广告。你将能够建立一个组织来为你做这些，即自主企业。现在我不确定它何时会发生，但它肯定会在未来五年内发生。所以这些是我们在应用层真正兴奋地追求的想法。至于前沿实验室会做什么，他们将在编码能力上继续攀登。很明显，这是模型取得进展的非常可靠的方式。而编码能力的所有进步都将转化为追求我刚才描述的应用，因为从根本上说，当你进入代码模式并暴露你的工具链时，一切都是为了向编码智能体暴露原语。所以那是你的工作。因此，当你构建基础设施、构建正确的原语时，你就可以在所有实验室将继续产生的能力上攀登。现在，在编码之外的事情上，我相信他们将在设计芯片、构建机器人和设计药物方面取得非常好的进展。也许应用层公司在那里可以发挥作用，如果他们在最后一公里问题上非常擅长，与实验室一起进行现场测试，或者能够真正在工厂部署机器人，或者拥有来自晶圆厂的大量数据，使你能够在真实的物理测量和测试上闭环，因为构建芯片时很多事物在模拟中可行，但当你把它们全部组装到机架中时，实际上并不一定可行。所以应用层公司可能有机会与前沿实验室合作，真正将他们设计的芯片投入实际生产。

turns.en: Let's talk about your customers. Where are you seeing the most growth with customers? Are you seeing enterprise demand inflect in certain use cases? Give us a sense for demand.
turns.zh: 我们来谈谈你们的客户。你们在哪里看到客户增长最快？你们是否看到企业需求在某些用例中出现拐点？给我们一个需求的感觉。

turns.en: So today this year has been really surprising to us that a lot of our revenue growth came from businesses, not users. Most of our users even on the consumer paid plans are actually people and companies. They're just using it out of their own accounts or they're just expensing it. But a lot of the revenue growth in terms of token consumption has come from businesses.
turns.zh: 所以今年到目前为止，让我们非常惊讶的是，我们很多收入增长来自企业，而不是用户。我们的大多数用户，即使在消费者付费计划上，实际上也是个人和公司。他们只是用自己的账户使用，或者只是报销。但就 token 消耗而言，很多收入增长来自企业。

turns.en: And that is largely coming from small and mid-market category today for us. Eventually, we believe that the same kind of demand that we're having for SEO and analysts, or ad campaign managers, or business analysts, corporate development, strategy, chief of staffs, admins—all these kinds of roles that are getting automated through our agent harness—we absolutely see that as something that we can replicate in large enterprises too. So that's going to be our focus for next year.
turns.zh: 目前这主要来自中小市场类别。最终，我们相信，就像我们现在对 SEO 和分析师、广告活动经理、业务分析师、企业发展、战略、参谋长、行政人员等角色的需求一样——所有这些角色都在通过我们的智能体框架实现自动化——我们绝对认为我们也可以在大型企业中复制这一点。所以这将是我们明年的重点。

turns.en: I want to transition into the topic of Jensen. So you were at Semaphore earlier this week. You said we need more Jensens in America, more founders like Jensen. Perplexity has had a strong relationship with NVIDIA. They've invested in several of your rounds. Jensen, you had said, was a Perplexity user. How does your relationship with NVIDIA evolve if Jensen's not in the seat? And separately, opine on how you think the AI ecosystem evolves, specifically on open models, what your thoughts are.
turns.zh: 我想过渡到 Jensen 的话题。你本周早些时候在 Semaphore 上说过，我们需要更多像 Jensen 这样的创始人。Perplexity 与 NVIDIA 有着牢固的关系。他们投资了你们的几轮融资。你曾说过 Jensen 是 Perplexity 的用户。如果 Jensen 不在位，你与 NVIDIA 的关系将如何演变？另外，请谈谈你认为 AI 生态系统如何演变，特别是关于开放模型，你的想法是什么。

turns.en: Yeah. So Jensen actually is exemplary in how he runs NVIDIA. Nobody can replicate that. That said, he always made sure that any of the partners that NVIDIA has is not just a partner in Jensen. He's always made us work with the rest of the team himself. Like we did not even ask for this. He's already connected us to a lot of VPs and directors and individual contributors. There's a lot of Slack channels we have with them together. Our engineers regularly sit on meetings with their engineers. Our marketing teams talk to each other. We're working with them on local deployments of our agent harness inside DGX and RPX park. We're regularly collaborating with them on open source releases. The sandbox platform space that powers our agents, we open sourced it and we took a lot of feedback from them. They had early access. And we also gave them feedback on their library Open Shell. We were one of the first to actually get access to various CPUs. That was through Ian Buck. And we shared our performance numbers on it. So the collaborations are actually pretty deep. And that's how it should be. And I'm pretty sure that other labs that work with NVIDIA structure the same way. Like I'm sure that they're already talking to a lot of internal people. And this is all thanks to how Jensen set it up. He's not about like oh this partner needs this, just give it to them. It's very meritorious. We earn our right to work with them by showing them some insightful results and then they see opportunity there to work together and make something new happen.
turns.zh: 是的。Jensen 在经营 NVIDIA 方面确实是典范。没有人能复制这一点。尽管如此，他总是确保 NVIDIA 的任何合作伙伴不仅仅是 Jensen 的合作伙伴。他总是让我们与团队的其他成员合作。就像我们甚至没有要求这个。他已经把我们与许多副总裁、总监和个体贡献者联系起来了。我们有很多 Slack 频道与他们一起。我们的工程师定期与他们的工程师开会。我们的营销团队互相交流。我们正在与他们合作，在 DGX 和 RPX park 内部本地部署我们的智能体框架。我们定期在开源发布上与他们合作。为我们的智能体提供支持的沙盒平台空间，我们将其开源，并从他们那里获得了很多反馈。他们获得了早期访问权。我们还对他们的库 Open Shell 提供了反馈。我们是首批获得各种 CPU 访问权的公司之一。那是通过 Ian Buck。我们分享了我们的性能数据。所以合作实际上相当深入。而且就应该这样。我确信其他与 NVIDIA 合作的实验室也是同样的结构。就像我确信他们已经在与许多内部人员交谈。这一切都归功于 Jensen 的设置方式。他不是那种‘哦，这个合作伙伴需要这个，就给他们’的人。这非常任人唯贤。我们通过向他们展示一些有洞察力的结果来赢得与他们合作的权利，然后他们看到机会一起合作，创造新事物。

turns.en: And then your thoughts on how the open model ecosystem could evolve?
turns.zh: 那么你对开放模型生态系统如何演变有何看法？

turns.en: I believe that the open source alliance that Jensen released a while ago, which we're happy to be part of, is what any company that put their logo on that should actually do meaningful work. It shouldn't be just NVIDIA, right? He's not even interested in just having NVIDIA be the only company doing open source. He wants every company in America to be an open source company. And in some sense, being an open source company is deeply an American thing to do. It supports the overall ecosystem. It allows other small businesses to operate more efficiently. People don't have to pay a fortune to access smart AI models. They can try new business ideas. So we are deeply committed to that. In fact, Jensen and NVIDIA pushed us to open source our sandbox platform space that so many Neo clouds are now going to take and put it on their compute clusters and sell access to other companies. We're going to do the same with all the models we're training. We're going to open source a lot of environments for agent harnesses to be post-trained effectively. So more and more open source being done by more people, be it on the pre-training side or post-training side or tooling or infrastructure is very essential to keep the whole thing going. And we should all continue in the footsteps of Jensen here.
turns.zh: 我相信 Jensen 不久前发布的那个开源联盟——我们很高兴成为其中一员——是任何贴上其标志的公司都应该真正做有意义的工作。不应该只是 NVIDIA，对吧？他甚至不感兴趣让 NVIDIA 成为唯一做开源的公司。他希望美国的每家公司都成为开源公司。在某种意义上，成为开源公司是深深植根于美国的事情。它支持整个生态系统。它允许其他小企业更高效地运营。人们不必支付巨额费用就能访问智能 AI 模型。他们可以尝试新的商业想法。所以我们对此深感承诺。事实上，Jensen 和 NVIDIA 推动我们将我们的沙盒平台空间开源，现在许多 Neo 云将采用它并将其放在他们的计算集群上，并向其他公司出售访问权限。我们将对我们训练的所有模型做同样的事情。我们将开源许多环境，以便智能体框架能够有效地进行后训练。所以越来越多的人做越来越多的开源，无论是在预训练方面还是后训练方面，或是工具或基础设施，对于保持整个事情运转至关重要。我们都应该继续追随 Jensen 的脚步。

turns.en: And just working as closely as you do with the American open source ecosystem, what do you think—Jensen was a big driver of that—Meta's open source Muse Spark. I think they may have said they may open source Wonder at some point. Did they say that?
turns.zh: 而且，正如你与美国开源生态系统密切合作一样，你认为——Jensen 是很大的推动者——Meta 的开源 Muse Spark。我想他们可能说过他们可能在某个时候开源 Wonder。他们说过吗？

turns.en: I think they've said that, but I hope they do.
turns.zh: 我想他们说过，但我希望他们真的做。

turns.en: And then we've got reflection with Beam. We've got Thinking Machines. How competitive if you look out six to nine months from now, is American open source ahead of Chinese open source?
turns.zh: 然后我们有 Reflection 的 Beam。我们有 Thinking Machines。如果你展望未来六到九个月，美国开源相对于中国开源有多大的竞争力？

turns.en: I hope so, and we're going to do our level best to make Neumitra on awesome, right? Nvidia is really one of the few companies extremely well positioned to keep investing in open source. The word Jensen uses, he would keep investing in open source for an eternity. And the reason for that is they are structurally positioned to benefit from that, and it also benefits the ecosystem. It's additive. And so we're going to obviously continue contributing there. Neumitron 35 VL was trained with a lot of our tokens, and we're going to continue doing that with Neumitron 4 as well. We're using and post-training Muse internally, testing it, running a lot of Evals on it, and we hope to release post-train versions of that. And anytime, it's very hard to be a serious player in this. I think Nvidia and Meta are so well positioned to shepherd American open source to be far better than Chinese and keep our ecosystem open and also the state of the art. That's the most important thing.
turns.zh: 我希望如此，我们将尽最大努力让 Neumitra 变得很棒，对吧？Nvidia 确实是少数几家处于极佳位置可以持续投资开源的公司之一。Jensen 用的词是，他会永远投资开源。原因在于他们从结构上就能从中受益，而且这也惠及生态系统。这是加法。所以我们显然会继续在那里贡献。Neumitron 35 VL 是用我们的大量 token 训练的，我们也将继续用 Neumitron 4 这样做。我们正在内部使用和后训练 Muse，测试它，运行大量评估，我们希望发布后训练版本。任何时候，要成为这个领域的严肃玩家都非常难。我认为 Nvidia 和 Meta 处于非常有利的位置，可以引领美国开源远远超越中国，保持我们的生态系统开放，同时也保持最先进水平。那是最重要的事情。

turns.en: And do you think that's realistic in six to nine months? You hope so, but do you think it's possible, probable?
turns.zh: 你认为这在六到九个月内现实吗？你希望如此，但你认为这可能吗， probable？

turns.en: I think so. I think so. Realistically, Muse is already very good. Now, can Muse be better than Deep Sea and GLM? Absolutely. They have so many great researchers, a lot of compute incentives to actually go and get a mind share in the developer ecosystem, and they can still monetize things with ads. So it's definitely possible.
turns.zh: 我认为如此。我认为如此。现实地说，Muse 已经非常好了。现在，Muse 能比 Deep Sea 和 GLM 更好吗？绝对可以。他们有这么多优秀的研究人员，大量的算力激励，实际上可以去在开发者生态系统中获得心智份额，而且他们仍然可以通过广告变现。所以这绝对是可能的。

turns.en: Well, let's hope it happens.
turns.zh: 好吧，让我们希望它发生。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: Yeah. Please, Stephanie.
turns.zh: 是的。请，Stephanie。

turns.en: Touching on the hyper scalers. So Google, Arvin, a little over a year ago, you did an interview where you made some pretty prescient comments about Google. You effectively said Google search margins should continue to degrade and Google's doing the right thing. Basically winning the loyalty of the user rather than the loyalty of the advertiser is the way to ultimately win. Has your view changed or feel free to add additional comments?
turns.zh: 谈谈超大规模企业。那么 Google，Arvin，一年多前，你接受了一次采访，对 Google 做出了一些非常有先见之明的评论。你实际上说 Google 搜索的利润率应该继续下降，而 Google 正在做正确的事情。基本上，赢得用户的忠诚而不是广告商的忠诚是最终获胜的方式。你的观点改变了吗？或者请随意补充评论。

turns.en: To be honest, I had a mental model that it would be hard for them to basically do perplexity inside the Google search bar. They did it and then nothing happened to the ad revenue for a few quarters.
turns.zh: 说实话，我之前的心理模型是，他们很难在 Google 搜索栏内基本上实现 Perplexity 的功能。他们做到了，然后广告收入在几个季度内没有发生任何变化。

turns.en: So I was like, okay, wait, what's going on? Did I have a wrong mental model of the world? But then the most recent earnings call, you got to see that they did take a hit on the acceleration of search ads because of AI mode, right? So it is zero sum. There's only certain real estate, and if you allocate it to clicking on links, you cannot put a really good AI answer that just gives you the answer. So they're going to obviously have to figure it out. And the best thing they could have done, honestly, is to just not ever roll it out. And that would have kept the search business alive, and they could keep investing in cloud. So this dilemma is always going to be there for them, and this is precisely why the innovator's dilemma is a real thing. And the same thing is going to be true for agents. If agents are actually going to go and make purchases on behalf of the user, how are you actually going to charge for humans to click on five different links and charge for the cost per click? It's very hard.
turns.zh: 所以我当时就想，等等，这是怎么回事？是不是我对世界的心智模型错了？但最近这次财报电话会议，你能看到他们确实因为 AI 模式在搜索广告增速上受了冲击，对吧？所以它确实是零和的。屏幕空间就那么大，如果你把它分配给点击链接，你就没法放一个真正好的、直接给你答案的 AI 回答。所以他们显然得想办法解决。说实话，他们能做的最好的事，就是干脆永远别推出。那样搜索业务还能活着，他们也能继续投资云。所以这个两难对他们来说会一直存在，而这正是为什么“创新者的窘境”是真实存在的。同样的事对智能体也成立。如果智能体真的替用户去买东西，你还怎么按人类点击五个不同链接来收费、按每次点击成本收费？这非常难。

turns.en: Do you think Google will figure it out?
turns.zh: 你觉得 Google 能解决这个问题吗？

turns.en: I'm happy that I don't have to do the job, so you know.
turns.zh: 我很庆幸自己不用干这活儿，所以你知道的。

turns.en: Fair enough. You're a student of business. You've also commented in the past around how Microsoft effectively disrupted itself and became a different company. Feel like this conversation around Google, we're seeing some of that as well. How have you disrupted Perplexity and the strategic roadmap thus far as the AI industry has changed? I mean, as you said, five years is effectively 10 to 15 years.
turns.zh: 有道理。你是研究商业的人。你过去也评论过微软如何有效地自我颠覆、变成了一家不同的公司。感觉围绕 Google 的这场讨论，我们也看到了一些类似的东西。随着 AI 行业的变化，你是如何颠覆 Perplexity 以及迄今为止的战略路线图的？我的意思是，就像你说的，五年实际上相当于 10 到 15 年。

turns.en: Yeah. So I wouldn't say really a disruption, it's more a transformation. When we saw towards the end of last year that Opus 4.5 and Claude Code — all our engineers immediately moved from Cursor to that. We could see how much of a different paradigm it was. We didn't just see that as, oh, that's coding and we're doing something else. What we basically saw was, okay, look, models are actually finally good at coding. We saw some traces of it with Sonnet 3.5 and things like that, but Opus 3.5 was a flop, it didn't work, and so people were waiting for it, and it finally happened with the 4.5 generation. So when we saw that, we were like, should we just ignore that trend and keep doing what we are doing, which is indexing the web and summarizing it, or should we actually build products that benefit from further advances there? If so much compute and researcher talent is going to be allocated to making whatever is Opus 4.5 three or four times better in the next 12 months, you want to benefit from those capabilities and think of products that actually benefit from that and create new experiences for people. And whatever was a local coding agent, imagine you put that on the cloud and make it do any task, not just coding. That was the key inspiration idea behind Perplexity Computer. And when we did that, obviously there were like 20 engineers working on it, the rest of the company was working on something else. And that particular period, we froze the code base, didn't ship anything for three to four months. A lot of people outside were wondering — there were some well-meaning people who even texted me saying, hey, hope you're all right and all that stuff, as if I disappeared completely from the face of the earth. So we came back and shipped Computer, and that changed our destiny forever. But that was deep conviction in the fact that models are going to be really good at code, code is going to be the way to do any kind of work — it doesn't matter whether it's software engineering or legal or insurance or accounting — and just make it extremely intuitive, that everything is abstracted out, runs on the cloud, and the user doesn't have to understand concepts like harnesses, dispatching jobs, and things like that. That's basically the problem we solved, and I'm sure we'll have to do more such things next year and so on. So in some sense, that is our job. Our job is to basically keep innovating, forecast where the frontier is going to be six months from now, and build products that would actually be okayish today and will be really good when that model lands six months from now.
turns.zh: 是的。我不会说这是颠覆，更像是转型。去年年底我们看到 Opus 4.5 和 Claude Code 时，我们所有工程师立刻从 Cursor 转了过去。我们能看出这是多么不同的范式。我们并没有把它看成“哦，那是写代码的事，我们在做别的”。我们真正看到的是：好吧，模型终于真的擅长写代码了。我们在 Sonnet 3.5 之类的模型上看到过一些苗头，但 Opus 3.5 是个失败，没成功，所以大家一直在等，终于在 4.5 这一代实现了。所以当我们看到这一点时，我们就在想：我们是该无视这个趋势、继续做我们正在做的事，也就是索引网络并做摘要，还是该去打造能从这些进一步进展中受益的产品？如果未来 12 个月有那么多算力和研究员人才被投入到把 Opus 4.5 之类的模型提升三四倍，你就想从这些能力中受益，去构思真正能从中获益、并为人们创造新体验的产品。原本是一个本地编码智能体，想象你把它放到云上，让它做任何任务，而不只是写代码。这就是 Perplexity Computer 背后的关键灵感。当我们做这件事时，显然有大约 20 名工程师在做它，公司其他人都在做别的事。那段时间我们冻结了代码库，三四个月没发布任何东西。外面很多人都在纳闷——有些好心人甚至给我发短信说，嘿，希望你一切都好之类的，好像我完全从地球上消失了一样。然后我们回来，发布了 Computer，那永远改变了我们的命运。但那是基于一种深深的信念：模型会在代码上变得非常强，代码会成为做任何工作的方式——不管是软件工程、法律、保险还是会计——并且要让它极其直观，一切都抽象掉、跑在云上，用户不必理解 harness、派发任务之类的概念。这基本上就是我们解决的问题，我相信明年以及以后我们还得做更多这样的事。所以某种意义上，这就是我们的工作。我们的工作就是持续创新，预测六个月后前沿会在哪里，并打造出今天还算可以、等六个月后那个模型落地时会非常出色的产品。

turns.en: What are your favorite internal Perplexity Computer use cases or your favorite agentic AI use cases at Perplexity? Like how differently do you run the company today relative to pre-Perplexity Computer?
turns.zh: 你最喜欢的 Perplexity Computer 内部用例，或者你在 Perplexity 最喜欢的智能体式 AI 用例是什么？比如，相比有 Perplexity Computer 之前，你今天经营公司的方式有多大不同？

turns.en: The biggest change is that most of my questions are now internal facing. I ask a lot of questions on why is this project moving slow, what are the real bottlenecks here. Like there is a certain bug I see on Twitter — earlier I would just paste the bug on Slack and ask somebody to fix it. Now I just have a teammate that does root cause analysis of the bug just from the Twitter URL and pages the right engineer. And I have teammates that do that all the time, running on my local browser, scanning Twitter for bugs. And I've made sure that every engineering team has set up automations like these. So the speed at which you can fix bugs based on what people post online has multiplied like 10 to 100x. And of course, the human still has to look at the PR the AI writes and make sure that the merges are done carefully, because at one point we merged the wrong PR and it cost us a lot of money. So we're still not quite there in terms of full recursive self-improvement style loops for a company. But that's what I imagined — like, you know, a few months from now, would that be possible where an AI can just scan for bugs online and just merge PRs on its own and verify that it actually ended up fixing the bug and it moved business metrics? Can I just point it at a certain retention metric and have a hill climb on it for like a few weeks, and itself make adjustments until it achieves the target? So all that stuff is—
turns.zh: 最大的变化是，我现在大多数问题都是对内的。我会问很多问题：这个项目为什么进展慢？真正的瓶颈在哪里？比如我在 Twitter 上看到某个 bug——以前我就把 bug 粘贴到 Slack 上，让人去修。现在我有一个队友，仅凭 Twitter 链接就做 bug 的根因分析，并呼叫对的工程师。我还有队友一直在做这件事，跑在我的本地浏览器上，扫描 Twitter 找 bug。而且我确保每个工程团队都设置了这样的自动化。所以根据人们在网上发的内容来修 bug 的速度，提升了 10 到 100 倍。当然，人还是得看 AI 写的 PR，确保合并做得小心，因为有一次我们合并了错误的 PR，损失了很多钱。所以我们在公司层面还没有完全达到那种完整的递归自我改进式循环。但那正是我想象的——你知道，几个月后，有没有可能让 AI 直接在网上扫描 bug，自己合并 PR，并验证它确实修好了 bug、推动了业务指标？我能不能直接把它指向某个留存指标，让它爬坡几周，自己做出调整直到达成目标？所以所有这些——

turns.en: Has that actually happened, what you just said?
turns.zh: 你刚说的那些，真的发生了吗？

turns.en: Not yet.
turns.zh: 还没有。

turns.en: Yeah, that's—
turns.zh: 是啊，那——

turns.en: Not yet. In fact—
turns.zh: 还没有。事实上——

turns.en: —be pretty amazing.
turns.zh: ——那会相当惊人。

turns.en: Yeah. And by the way, there are a lot of real world bottlenecks. Like while you run an AB test, there'll be somebody else running an AB test that overlaps on the same segment of user, and AI is not very good at causal analysis. So it's not like we're truly there at a recursive business, but we are trying to see what are all the blind spots and—
turns.zh: 是的。顺便说一句，现实世界有很多瓶颈。比如你在跑一个 AB 测试时，会有别人也在跑一个 AB 测试，覆盖同一批用户，而 AI 并不太擅长因果分析。所以并不是说我们真的已经实现了递归式业务，但我们正试图找出所有的盲点，而且——

turns.en: Can you compare and contrast using Opus 5.5 in Perplexity Computer with the experience of using it in its native harness, which I guess is co-work these days?
turns.zh: 你能对比一下在 Perplexity Computer 里用 Opus 5.5，和在它原生 harness 里用的体验吗？我猜现在那个叫 co-work？

turns.en: Co-work, yeah. Actually, Dylan Patel spoke about this, so you can trust his word over mine.
turns.zh: 对，co-work。其实 Dylan Patel 讲过这个，所以你可以信他胜过信我。

turns.en: SemiAnalysis, a mega Perplexity fan. But share his—
turns.zh: SemiAnalysis，Perplexity 的超级粉丝。但说说他的——

turns.en: He's not an investor. He has no stake in our company. I'm not paying him. He basically has really demanding people. That firm is incredible. They just ping us at 1 a.m. on Friday nights, Saturday nights, asking for features, and we like it because that way I can push my engineers to also work harder. They've been using Perplexity Computer as a Slack bot, and they really just want to work in Slack. They don't even want to go to any AI interface, like any Mac app or web. They just want to work in Slack. They just want to talk to the AI like a coworker and keep delegating tasks to it and take the outputs and keep refining. And ours is the best agent in that sort of setting compared to any other agent out there. And Dylan himself said it's kind of funny because they use the models, but they make the model so much better, so much more accurate, so much more reliable. And that's an artifact of us using multi-model and multi-agent orchestration, because if you make your harness good for any model, you end up making it very reliable, very robust. So any changes to the model do not truly affect you. That's basically the benefit.
turns.zh: 他不是投资人，在我们公司没有股份，我也没付他钱。他手下的人要求特别高，那家公司很厉害。他们会在周五晚上、周六凌晨 1 点给我们发消息要功能，我们还挺喜欢，因为这样我也能逼着工程师更努力。他们一直把 Perplexity Computer 当 Slack 机器人用，就是想在 Slack 里干活，根本不想打开任何 AI 界面，不管是 Mac 应用还是网页。他们就想在 Slack 里像跟同事一样跟 AI 说话，不断派活、拿结果、继续打磨。在这种场景下，我们的智能体比市面上任何其他智能体都强。Dylan 自己说，有意思的是他们用的是那些模型，但他们让模型变得好得多、准确得多、可靠得多。这是我们采用多模型、多智能体编排的结果：如果你的 harness 对任何模型都好用，它最终就会非常可靠、非常稳健，模型的任何变化都影响不到你。这就是好处。

turns.en: Can you talk a little bit about your customer base since you turned on Perplexity Computer? Like what are the three biggest industries? How big are the companies?
turns.zh: 能聊聊你开启 Perplexity Computer 之后的客户群吗？比如最大的三个行业是什么？公司规模有多大？

turns.en: Yeah. So I would say in descending order: finance, legal, and basic corporate strategy and development, web app building, e-commerce, small and mid-market companies that are short of labor. This is where we're seeing real demand today. That's what's contributed to our revenue. But most of these things are replicable in a larger company as well, starting with small teams inside large companies to eventually the whole company. So our goal is: whatever we did this year, where we grew our headcount hardly by like 10 or 20% but grew our revenue by four to 5X, our goal is to give that power to every other company on the planet, and that is Perplexity. Our company runs on our own product. That's how we fix all our bugs really fast. The reason SemiAnalysis is able to benefit from it is because we're giving them the same thing that we're using. So every time we improve the product for ourselves, our own company, it improves our product for every other company. And of course, there's going to be some inertia in adopting it in larger enterprises, but eventually we're going to figure that out and that's going to translate to a lot of value.
turns.zh: 好。按降序说：金融、法律，以及基础的企业战略与业务发展、网页应用搭建、电商，还有缺人手的中小企业。这些是我们今天看到真实需求的领域，也是我们营收的来源。但其中大多数事情在大公司里同样可以复制，从大公司内部的小团队开始，最终扩展到整个公司。所以我们的目标是：我们今年员工人数只增长了大概 10% 到 20%，营收却增长了 4 到 5 倍，我们要把这种能力给到地球上每一家公司，这就是 Perplexity。我们公司就运行在自己的产品上，所以我们修 bug 特别快。SemiAnalysis 能从中受益，是因为我们给他们的就是我们自己在用的东西。每当我们为自己公司改进产品，也就为其他所有公司改进了产品。当然，大企业在采用上会有一些惯性，但最终我们会解决这个问题，那会转化为巨大的价值。

turns.en: What is the go-to-market?
turns.zh: 那市场推广策略是什么？

turns.en: What is the go-to-market for those large enterprises? Are you going to hire sales reps or what?
turns.zh: 对那些大企业的市场推广怎么做？你们打算招销售代表还是怎样？

turns.en: Yeah, we are actively hiring. We've already 5 to 6X'd our sales team headcount in the last three months. We had five reps at the beginning of the year. That's it.
turns.zh: 对，我们在积极招人。过去三个月我们的销售团队人数已经翻了 5 到 6 倍。年初我们只有五个销售代表，就这么多。

turns.en: Wow.
turns.zh: 哇。

turns.en: So now we have like 20 to 30. So we are hiring very fast. But of course, time to ramp up a rep, all that stuff matters too. Revenue per rep is still pretty high in Perplexity. Time to ramp, time to close up first deals around 30 to 60 days. So one of the things we are trying to do is basically have them use agents all the time. Figure out the right deal to focus on, triage any new inbound to the right rep based on the history of deals they're working on. All that stuff is going to help us run far more efficiently than a typical sales organization. That's my hope. There are obviously real world bottlenecks: no matter which rep you put, you have to pass through the security reviews. You have to get comfortable with signing seven figure contracts. All that stuff is hard earned work that we just have to do. There's no shortcuts here. But the fact that our product is already a well-known brand, people already appreciate what it can do for orchestration. People already understand that it's model neutral. People can have an AI budget in their head and spend it all on one harness without feeling a model or vendor lock-in. And that way they maintain their automations, their tools, their sessions, memory, enterprise context and brain in a model agnostic fashion. So that's what we're going to sell. And that allows us to charge a markup on all the token price of the frontier models. Because frontier models are going to do the opposite. They're going to try to subsidize their tokens in their products, lock you into one model and one harness and not allow you to try multiple different models. So we want to charge a markup on those tokens, but we're going to completely make the switching cost between models zero. So it's a differentiated business model.
turns.zh: 现在大概有 20 到 30 人，招得很快。当然，销售代表的爬坡时间这些也很重要。Perplexity 的人均销售营收仍然相当高，爬坡时间、敲定第一单大概要 30 到 60 天。所以我们想做的一件事，就是让他们一直用智能体：找出该重点跟进的单子，根据他们手头单子的历史，把新的线索分派给合适的销售代表。这些都能帮我们比典型销售组织高效得多，这是我的期望。当然现实中有瓶颈：不管你派哪个销售代表，都得过安全审查，都得习惯签七位数的合同。这些都是必须硬啃的活，没有捷径。但我们的产品已经是知名品牌，人们已经认可它在编排上的能力，也明白它是模型中立的。人们可以在心里定一个 AI 预算，全花在一个 harness 上，而不用担心被某个模型或厂商锁定。这样他们就能以模型无关的方式保留自己的自动化、工具、会话、记忆、企业上下文和大脑。这就是我们要卖的东西。这也让我们能对前沿模型的 token 价格加价。因为前沿模型会反着来：它们会试图在自己的产品里补贴 token，把你锁在一个模型、一个 harness 上，不让你尝试多个不同模型。所以我们要对这些 token 加价，但我们会把模型之间的切换成本完全降为零。这是一个差异化的商业模式。

turns.en: I'm going to steal Gavin's thunder and ask his question: how do you see AI benefiting the ordinary American? And feel free to give an example of how you've seen your product benefit the ordinary American.
turns.zh: 我要抢 Gavin 的风头，问他的问题：你觉得 AI 会怎样让普通美国人受益？也欢迎举个例子，说说你看到你的产品如何让普通美国人受益。

turns.en: So AI will make America even more American. And fundamentally what it means to be an American is to not feel like you have any barriers. That's how I felt when I came into this country. There is this word people use, the American dream. I'm really living it right now. I had no right to be here sitting on the stage with people like you here or people in the stage watching me speak. I came here as a PhD student and I wasn't even approved a credit card by Bank of America. I had to wait for 4 months to get a credit score. So AI truly removes the barriers for anybody because all they need to be able to do is ask good questions, have agency, be able to come up with business ideas and have the discipline and the hard work to follow through all their ideas. And AI makes it so easy to actually execute these things. And so fundamentally I feel like if every American can go spin up a new business, do their own research and keep hill climbing on the progress, that's going to be great for the economy and that's really what the American dream is about.
turns.zh: AI 会让美国更像美国。从根本上说，身为美国人就意味着不觉得自己有任何壁垒。我刚来这个国家时就是这种感觉。人们常说一个词，美国梦，我现在真的活在其中。我本来没资格站在这个台上，和你们这样的人在一起，或者让台下的人听我讲话。我是以博士生身份来的，美国银行连信用卡都不批给我，我得等四个月才有信用分。所以 AI 真正为任何人移除了壁垒，因为他们只需要会问好问题、有主动性、能想出商业点子，并且有纪律和苦干精神把想法贯彻到底。而 AI 让真正执行这些事情变得非常容易。所以从根本上我觉得，如果每个美国人都能创办新生意、自己做研究、不断向上攀登，那对经济会非常好，而这正是美国梦的意义。

turns.en: It's a great answer. I almost want to end on that. I have one other question. Aravind, you have said in the past you would consider an IPO in the first half of 2027. Is that still fair game?
turns.zh: 这个回答很棒，我差点就想以此收尾了。我还有一个问题。Aravind，你过去说过会考虑在 2027 年上半年 IPO。这还算数吗？

turns.en: 2028 is our mental model.
turns.zh: 2028 年才是我们心里的时间点。

turns.en: Business is progressing faster. 650 million ARR was what I wanted to hit for the end of the year. We are tracking way above that because we just crossed a billion. So if the business progress sustains, we might consider filing sooner.
turns.zh: 业务进展比预期更快。6.5 亿美元的 ARR 是我原本想在年底达到的目标。我们现在的进度远超这个数字，因为我们刚刚突破 10 亿美元。所以如果业务进展能持续下去，我们可能会考虑更早提交上市申请。

turns.en: Great.
turns.zh: 太好了。

turns.en: Be excited to have you as a public company.
turns.zh: 很期待看到你成为一家上市公司。

turns.en: I hope so.
turns.zh: 希望如此。

turns.en: Don't be scared, Aravind. Public markets, it's great. People are too scared of them.
turns.zh: 别害怕，Aravind。公开市场很好。人们太害怕它了。

turns.en: Yeah, look. I mean public markets force you to be more disciplined, more rigorous. And we all need that because we've invested a lot in — I mean the whole markets think there's been a lot of investments in AI and where is the ROI. And companies like ourselves and so many other companies, not just us, Anthropic will not be the last IPO, right?
turns.zh: 是啊，你看。我的意思是，公开市场会迫使你更加自律、更加严谨。我们都需要这一点，因为我们在 AI 上投入了很多——整个市场都在想，AI 领域投了这么多钱，回报在哪里。像我们这样的公司，还有很多其他公司，不只是我们，Anthropic 不会是最后一家 IPO 的公司，对吧？

turns.en: Of course.
turns.zh: 当然。

turns.en: So that's going to be a lot more amazing IPOs coming up, and not everything needs to be a trillion-dollar IPO.
turns.zh: 所以接下来还会有很多很棒的 IPO，而且不是每家公司都需要做成万亿美元级别的 IPO。

turns.en: Of course. When do you think you'll start generating cash?
turns.zh: 当然。你觉得你们什么时候会开始产生现金流？

turns.en: Hopefully towards the end of next year.
turns.zh: 希望是在明年年底前后。

turns.en: Towards the end of next year?
turns.zh: 明年年底前后？

turns.en: Yes.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: Yeah. I'd recommend going public once you're generating cash. Yeah.
turns.zh: 嗯。我建议等你们开始产生现金流之后再上市。是的。

turns.en: Yes. Well, not every company has needed that as a constraint, but I'll take your recommendation. You're more experienced than me.
turns.zh: 好。不过也不是每家公司都把这一点当作硬性约束，但我会接受你的建议。你比我有经验。

turns.en: I want only good things for you, Aravind. Well, listen, Stephanie, thank you. You did an amazing job. Aravind, thank you so much. This was awesome. Thank you.
turns.zh: 我只希望你好，Aravind。好了，Stephanie，谢谢你。你做得非常棒。Aravind，非常感谢你。这次访谈太精彩了。谢谢。

turns.en: Thank you. Thanks everyone.
turns.zh: 谢谢。谢谢大家。

consensus.en: Every step an agent takes—picking tools, files, sources—is fundamentally a search problem.
consensus.zh: 智能体每一步——选工具、选文件、选来源——本质上都是搜索问题。

consensus.en: Perplexity's edge is accuracy from its own index plus model-neutral orchestration.
consensus.zh: Perplexity 的优势在于自有索引带来的准确性，加上模型中立的编排能力。

consensus.en: We stay capital efficient by doing post-training only, never pre-training.
consensus.zh: 我们只做后训练、不做预训练，以此保持资本高效。

consensus.en: Revenue grew 4.7x year over year, driven largely by business customers.
consensus.zh: 营收同比增长 4.7 倍，增长主要来自企业客户。

consensus.en: Build products that are okay today but excellent when the next frontier model lands.
consensus.zh: 打造今天尚可、等下一代前沿模型落地后变得出色的产品。

consensus.en: AI removes barriers, letting ordinary Americans start businesses and execute ideas.
consensus.zh: AI 消除壁垒，让普通美国人能创业并把想法落地。

contrarian.en: Search is not dead; it is the core primitive that makes agents trustworthy.
contrarian.zh: 搜索没有死；它恰恰是让智能体变得可信的核心基础能力。

contrarian.en: We benefit from every lab's progress and oppose banning open-weight models.
contrarian.zh: 我们从各家实验室的进步中获益，反对封禁开放权重模型。

contrarian.en: Google should never have rolled out AI answers; the innovator's dilemma is real.
contrarian.zh: 谷歌本就不该推出 AI 答案；创新者窘境是真实存在的。

contrarian.en: Frontier labs will subsidize tokens and lock users in; we charge a markup but make switching free.
contrarian.zh: 前沿实验室会补贴 token 并锁定用户；我们收取加价，但让切换成本归零。

contrarian.en: Trajectory efficiency—cost per whole agent session—matters more than cost per token.
contrarian.zh: 轨迹效率——整个智能体会话的成本——比每 token 成本更重要。

contrarian.en: Not every company needs to be a trillion-dollar IPO; many great IPOs are coming.
contrarian.zh: 并非每家公司都要做成万亿美元 IPO；未来会有很多优秀的 IPO。
